name: Ui_SakusenWindow_OpenCommandPane
signature: void Ui_SakusenWindow_OpenCommandPane(UiSakusenWindow *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: State handler run after a script callback returns: once the widget tick reports idle it advances the window's command queue, reads the queue entry id and pushes the matching command pane, playing the pane's SEs. Entry id 0 opens the two-pane (detail) layout; any other id collects the availability SEs 0x5A and 0x5C..0x60 for the four command slots and opens the single-pane layout.
evidence: Named callees now place it squarely in the tactics window: Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt (0x6D7F34) and Ui_SakusenWindow_PushPane (0x6D7FE8), and the queue/pane fields it uses (self+0x120, self+0x1140) are the same ones Ui_SakusenWindow_CloseDetail and Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry use. The old Ui_CommandWindow_ prefix was the wrong subsystem and 'Advance' hid that the visible effect is pushing a pane.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CloseDetail
summary: Closes the tactics window's detail view: hides the extra member row of the embedded status-parameter view at self+0x6E4, and, when the battle work reports nothing pending, releases the child screen and selects the fixed follow-up command entry.
evidence: The first callee is now named maybe_Ui_StatusParamWindow_ToggleMemberRow (0x3F1D48) and is called on self+0x6E4, exactly the 'hide the member row' half of closing the detail view, followed by Ui_ReleaseChildScreen and Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry with the constant pair at 0x72A610 - the same 'close and go to command X' sequence as the other Sakusen handlers.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdatePaneCommand
summary: Per-frame handler of one tactics-window state: ticks the window widget and, when the tick reports idle, selects the command entry whose id/flags are the constant pair in the literal pool. It does not pop or push anything itself, so which state it drives stays unknown.
evidence: The only named neighbour, Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry, is a 'find/select entry' call, not the queue advance the twin handlers use, so 'UpdatePaneCommand' is a vague but not wrong description; the literal-pool pair that would identify the state is aliased to the same address (0x0072A610) in the decompiled body and cannot be resolved from the readable C.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdatePaneCommandB
summary: Second per-frame handler of the same shape as 0x002A2820 (tick the widget, then select a fixed command entry when idle), registered at another slot of the Sakusen handler table; the constant pair that distinguishes the two states is not recoverable from the readable C.
evidence: Same body as 0x002A2820 and the same single named callee Ui_CommandQueue_FindEntry; the differing literal pair sits at 0x002A3098 but Ghidra aliased both references to 0x0072A610, so the state cannot be told apart.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_SwitchDetailPane
summary: Handles the tactics window's page/detail switch: on the input flag it forwards the input to the pane group at +0xAF4 and flips the visible detail pane (alternating +0xB4C between the two pane states at +0xAF4), and it always mirrors 'pane 0 shown' into the engine's detail-open byte at work+0x27C65 before advancing the command queue.
evidence: Confirmed as a Sakusen state handler: it uses the same event-flag dispatch (self->f_174) as Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateDetailPane/OnInputEx and calls the named Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt (0x6D7F34) on the same queue at self+0x120. The two-pane alternation (index+2)%2 on the group at +0xAF4 and the engine bool written from (f_B4C == 0) match the 'flip to the other detail pane' behaviour the old name claimed.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_OnInputEx
signature: void Ui_SakusenWindow_OnInputEx(UiSakusenWindow *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Input handler for the member/tactic list at self+0xB6C: on the accept flag it shows the row cursor, checks the per-row availability table at 0x0072D430 and, for a real member row (index < 4), keeps the cursor visible and scrolls the list to it; on the cancel flag with the list's fifth row (index 4) selected it clears the UI mode word and advances the command queue.
evidence: Neighbours are all input/cursor code: maybe_Ui_List_GetSelectionIndex on the list at +0xB6C, the cursor child at +0xE88 driven through vtable slot 0x18 (show/hide), and the scroll setter 0x001A6680 - the same trio used by the other Sakusen state handlers that react to the self->f_174 event bits, which supports 'input handler' rather than 'update'.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateWithPreCall
summary: Variant of the tactics-window update that first invokes virtual slot 0x78 on the owned object at +0x10E4 (an animation/effect tick), then ticks the widget and advances the command queue when the tick completes.
evidence: Only the two generic widget helpers (Ui_Widget_Update, the AdvanceAlt queue call) are named; the object at +0x10E4 and the purpose of its slot 0x78 are still unknown, so the handler's state cannot be named.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdatePopCommand
summary: Per-frame handler: ticks the window widget and, when the tick reports idle, advances (not pops) the command queue at self+0x120 via Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt.
evidence: The queue callee is now named Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt ('advance'), which is not a pop; the name is otherwise still the best description of the body, so it stays a maybe_ with the corrected wording in the summary.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdatePopCommandB
summary: Second instance of the same tick-then-advance handler as 0x002A309C, registered at another slot of the Sakusen handler table next to Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateSelectedIcon.
evidence: Identical instruction sequence to 0x002A309C (Ui_Widget_Update + idle gate + Ui_CommandQueue_AdvanceAlt); only the table slot differs, so the state it serves is unknown and the name stays a maybe_.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_UpdateDetailPane
summary: Switches the tactics window's detail area to match the selected entry: on the input flag it feeds the input to the pane group at +0xA40 and relabels the sub-window at +0xA8C with the entry kind; on the confirm flag, kind 0 shows the member child at +0xB6C (after rebuilding the bag context) and kind 1 shows the parameter child at +0xAF4.
evidence: The relabel callee is now named maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_SetCommandLabel (0x4DCED0) and is called on the sub-window with the selected entry's kind byte, matching UpdateSelectedIcon's 'kind selects the pane' behaviour; the two children it shows (+0xB6C, +0xAF4) are the same two the input/switch handlers use, so 'UpdateDetailPane' is exactly what the body does.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_SetSlotVisibility
summary: Refreshes the eight equipment slots of the window from an 8-byte kind mask: each slot gets the icon resolved from its mask value (0xFF = empty icon), the used-slot count is recomputed and the six 0x14-byte slot frames are shown/hidden in a switch on that count.
evidence: The eight-slot loop over a kind mask with 0xFF as 'empty' and the per-count pane enable/disable still read as an equipment slot refresh, and the helpers 0x3E043C / 0x65D3A0 are now known layout-element calls, but the body carries a damaged argument register (in_d8) and the 'window' identity is only inferred from the eight equipment ids, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: Container_NamedMap_EraseEntryForKey
summary: Erases the name-keyed-map entry for one key before it is replaced: looks the node up with the same 9-word hash/name key as the insert path and, if a node exists, destroys the stored key string at +0x30 and unlinks the node from the red-black tree; returns 1 when something was erased.
evidence: Its only caller Container_NamedMap_Insert (0x002ACAA4, confidence 0.50) calls it first and then re-implements the identical FindNodeA + std_RbTree_EraseNode sequence inline, which shows the function is the 'drop the existing entry with this key' half of the insert, not a string update; the key layout (f_54..f_78, hash 0x782534) and the tree at self+0x18 match the insert exactly.

name: Ui_ScreenController_InitChildren
summary: Builds the child screen objects of a big UI screen controller: allocates and constructs fifteen children of different classes (0x94, 0x10C, 0xC0, 0x26C ... 0x5F0 bytes) into f_C..f_44, activates the initially selected child through its vtable slot 8 and runs the shared post-init.
evidence: Every allocation is now followed by a named constructor from the same UI family (maybe_Ui_CompositeObject_Ctor, maybe_Ui_SceneObject_Ctor_77AE08, maybe_Ui_ScreenChild_StatusObject_Ctor, maybe_Ui_ArcListWindow_CtorEmbedded ...), all constructed with 'self' as owner, and the tail activates child f_6C through vtable+8 - that is initialising the controller's children.

name: maybe_Ui_PartSlot_InitEmbedded
summary: Constructor for an embedded UI element that owns two animation-reference lists: installs the class vtable, zeroes the owner word, constructs the first anim-ref list in place, chains its two intrusive list heads to themselves and copies the default timing/owner words, then returns the enclosing object base (the passed pointer sits 0x58 bytes into it).
evidence: The callee is now named Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor (0x3E0454) and is called twice, so the body is a constructor of an object with two anim-ref lists; the returned pointer is 0x58 before the argument, i.e. this is the 'construct the base sub-object' member. Which class owns it is still unknown (the PartSlot label is the first pass's guess), so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipPart_Ctor
summary: Constructor of one part object of the equip window: installs the class vtable and the C++ static-init guard, copies the three default size triples, clears the three 0xC-byte sub-blocks and constructs the child animation-reference list at +0x6C.
evidence: The only caller is now named maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_InitSubParts (0x3331A8), which describes itself as chaining the part constructors at 0x002B28A4 four times, and the body writes a vtable at offset 0 - so 'InitDefaults' was the wrong role (it is a constructor), but the exact part class is still unknown.

name: Ui_WindowFrame_ApplySkin
summary: Applies the window-frame skin for the current frame phase: reads the 7-byte phase table at +0x54 (0xFFFF = no frame), resolves the border texture for the phase and the next phase (id table at 0x0072CC98) into the sprite at +0x28, and then sets the visible bit of each of the sixteen border parts at +0x60..+0xA8 according to the phase - corners for phases 0/2/3/6, the two side pairs for 3/4/5, the seam pieces only for phase 1. Phases 4 and 5 additionally swap the frame texture to ids 0xA1/0xA2.
evidence: The two callees are now known: Ui_GetCore (UI core, texture context at +0x10) and func_00633560 as the texture resolver called with ids 0xA1/0xA2, and the same 'visible' bit convention (bit 0 of +0x44) is used by the named sprite setter. Together with the per-phase part table this is exactly 'apply the skin/border style for the current frame phase', which is what the old name claimed.

name: maybe_Ui_Pane_CreateEffectForItemId
summary: Rebuilds the effect a pane shows from an item id: hides the current effect, resolves the item row (Item_LookupRecord, 0xB3B rows), takes its name string and creates/assigns the named UI effect into the pane's handle pair at +0x124.
evidence: The id lookup is the named Item_LookupRecord, so the argument is an item id, not a text id; the callers (maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyIconStyles, Ui_MessageWindow_SetTextId) use it to give a message window the icon of an item, and the second callee is now named maybe_Ui_Effect_Create. The old 'ForTextId' wording was misleading but the effect-creation role is confirmed, so it stays a maybe_ and only the wording changes.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageCmd_Apply
summary: Small dispatch adapter used by the message-window icon styling: when the command object has a handler (self[1]) and the id resolves to an item row, it rebuilds the item record and passes it to the object's virtual handler at slot 0.
evidence: Both lookups are the named Item_LookupRecord, so the id being applied is an item id and the callers are the message-window style/text setters; the object at self[0] is a plain handler (vtable slot 0 receives the 12-byte record), which fits the vague 'cmd' label but does not identify the class.

name: maybe_Ui_MonsterBook_EntryDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a monster-book entry row: installs the given vtable, releases the two links of the embedded node block and the two pack handles, runs the UI base destructor and then frees the storage.
evidence: The three callees are now all named - Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles, Pack_ReleaseHandle and Ui_Object_DtorBase - plus the trailing free, which is the textbook deleting-destructor shape (free). The entry/monster-book identity still rests on the first pass's vtable guess, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_MonsterBook_EntryDtorB
summary: Non-deleting twin of 0x00419EC8: the same vtable install, node-block unlink, two pack-handle releases and UI base destructor, but it keeps the storage (no free call) - the destructor variant the compiler emits for stack/embedded objects.
evidence: Identical body to 0x00419EC8 with the named Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles / Pack_ReleaseHandle / Ui_Object_DtorBase calls and without the trailing free, confirming the dtor pair; only the class label is still unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IconTableDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the small icon-table window built by 0x002BB660: installs the vtable, releases the handle pair at +0x124 and runs Ui_Object_DtorBase on the enclosing object, then frees it.
evidence: The helpers are now named Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles and Ui_Object_DtorBase and the trailing free confirms this is the deleting variant of the pair; the class identity still comes only from the constructor at 0x002BB660, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IconTableDtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the same icon-table window: identical vtable install, handle-pair release at +0x124 and Ui_Object_DtorBase call as 0x002BB758, without the free, so the object's storage is left to the caller.
evidence: Same first half as 0x002BB758 with the same named helpers and no free tail; confirms the (deleting, non-deleting) dtor pair, class label still unverified.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_SubObjectDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the tactics-window sub-object: restores its two vtable words (0x759388 / 0x760648), unlinks the embedded intrusive lists, clears the owner's back-pointer, releases the two child handles through their UI base destructors and frees the block.
evidence: It is the exact mirror of the constructor 0x003193BC (same vtable pair and the same 0x1CC-byte payload) and its callees are now named Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles and Ui_Object_DtorBase, followed by the free - a deleting destructor whose class is the one the ctor builds.

name: Field_Gimmick_Update
summary: Per-frame update (a vtable slot of the field gimmick, next to the scene-node methods): steps the gimmick's animation frame while a marker is visible, clamps the scene object to the marker/record position and tests collision, tears the effect nodes down when the marker disappears, and finally plays the animation that matches the current direction byte.
evidence: Callees now named: Field_Gimmick_StepAnimFrame (0x2BDECC), Field_SceneNode_PlayAnimation, maybe_Field_Gimmick_ClampObjectPosition, maybe_Gfx_ReleaseEffectNodes, plus the Os_GetGameWork -> +0x54/+0x48 UI-overlay reads; the eight-way direction switch feeding PlayAnimation is the per-frame behaviour of an update slot, so 'Update' is the right role name.

name: Pack_HandlePair_ResetAndGetBase
summary: Clears a two-word generation-tagged handle pair: zeroes the owner word, releases the entries of the second word through the pack handle table (0x7BA2D0) and writes the 'null' encoding 0xFFFFF000, then returns the address just before the pair - the enclosing element - so the caller can go on tearing that down.
evidence: The generation check (0xFFFFF / table 0x7BA2D0) is the same one Pack_ReleaseHandle and Pack_FreeHandleEntry use, both now named, and the only caller is Ui_DiveStartWindow_Dtor (0x32C1AC) - a destructor clearing handle pairs, which contradicts the first pass's 'PreDiveText' idea; the -4 return is the same 'element base' idiom as Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles.

name: Pack_HandlePair_Reset
summary: Void variant of 0x003E9DC0: zeroes the owner word of a two-word handle pair, releases the handle stored in the second word when its generation still matches the table entry and writes the pair's null encoding.
evidence: Same body as 0x003E9DC0 minus the returned base pointer, with the named Pack_FreeHandleEntry / Pack_ReleaseHandle generation check; its caller Ui_DiveStartWindow_Dtor uses it to clear the window's handle pairs, so the generic pack handle-pair reset is the honest name instead of the old PreDiveText guess.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveStartWindow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting-destructor thunk of the dive-start window: installs the class vtable passed in the second argument, runs the window's destructor body at 0x0032C1AC and frees the object.
evidence: The teardown callee 0x0032C1AC is now named Ui_DiveStartWindow_Dtor, and *self = vtable; DtorBody(self); free(self) is the deleting-destructor shape, so Container_DtorAndFree was only a structural description. It stays a maybe_ because 0x00304F34 already carries the name Ui_DiveStartWindow_DeletingDtor for the fully inlined D0 of that class - this small thunk either is a second emission or the D0 of a derived class whose base teardown is 0x0032C1AC; the mix-up is not resolvable here.

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderObject_ReleaseBindings
summary: Drops the three resource bindings a render object holds when their owners are gone: the texture binding at +0x68 (when +0x90 is clear), the material binding reached through +0x94 (when +0x28 is set and +0x30 is clear) and the material set through +0x98 (when +0x20 is set and +0x28 is clear).
evidence: The three callees are now named Gfx_TextureBinding_Release, Gfx_MaterialBinding_Release and Gfx_MaterialSet_Release, so the function releases resource bindings, not 'cached lists' as the first pass guessed. The body still uses an unrecovered argument register (unaff_r4, thumb entry, no readable caller), so the object type and the name stay a maybe_ with low confidence.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneObject_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor body of a multi-base scene object: installs the class vtable and then, for each embedded base at -0x38, -0x6C and -0x98 relative to the binding block, restores that base's vtable (0x782198 / 0x7821A8) and releases its material/texture binding, finally running the root destructor at 0x5F8528.
evidence: The calls that looked like 'init' are now named Gfx_MaterialBinding_Release / Gfx_TextureBinding_Release and each is preceded by a base-vtable store, which is the standard sequence for destroying embedded bases - so 'ConstructSubObjects/InitSubObjects' had the direction wrong. Its twin 0x002C6A0C is the deleting variant (it adds the free).

name: Ui_DataPanel_OpenDefault
signature: void Ui_DataPanel_OpenDefault(DataPanel *self, u8 mode, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Opens a data panel in its default state: clears the busy byte, resets the game window's shared state, re-initialises the panel's party snapshot, stores the requested mode, switches the panel state machine to state 3 and takes the panel's mutex before the caller fills it.
evidence: The callees are now named - Ui_Window_ResetState (0x35F814), Save_InitPartySnapshot (0x10F3E0) and Os_MutexLock - so the body is the 'reset everything, set mode, enter state 3, lock' opening sequence; the panel identity comes from the 0xE400-byte data-panel block the family shares (f_E0F4/f_E110/f_E3C4).

name: Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPathA
signature: int Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPathA(void *obj, u32 fmtArg, void *pathMethod, u32 methodOffset, void *dest)
summary: Loads one resource file whose path is produced by a virtual method of `obj`: calls that method into a 264-byte path buffer, converts the multibyte path to UTF-16, splits the device path and reads the file into the caller's destination buffer through Fs_Object_ReadAll (this instantiation copies 0x14 bytes), releasing the temporary file object on every path.
evidence: The whole tail is the named file-system chain Fs_SplitResourceName / Fs_ClassifyResult / Fs_Object_ReadAll / Fs_Object_ReleaseHandle, whose description explicitly mentions 'the save layer's status enum', and its only caller is the save-slot loader 0x002CD02C loading into save+0xe0e0 - no message or text system is involved, so the first pass's 'Ui_Message_FormatText' was wrong.

name: Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPathB
signature: int Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPathB(void *obj, u32 fmtArg, void *pathMethod, u32 methodOffset, void *dest)
summary: Second instantiation of the file loader (same code, different literal pool): builds the path through the object's virtual method, converts it to UTF-16 and reads the file into the destination - this copy transfers 0x1828 bytes - with the same Fs result classification and handle release.
evidence: Instruction-identical to 0x006D909C except the pool constants; the only difference in behaviour is the transfer size (0x14 vs 0x1828), which is exactly the two file sizes the save-slot loader 0x002CD02C needs, and all callees in the tail are named Fs_* file-system helpers.

name: Save_LoadSlotData
summary: Loads one save slot into the panel object: reads the small 0x14-byte slot header into save+8 and the 0xC8B0-byte party snapshot into save+0x1830, then the trailing 0x1828-byte block into save+0xE0E0, converting the path through the slot's virtual name method and aborting with the Fs status if any read fails.
evidence: The two format helpers are now identified as file loaders (Fs_Object_LoadByVirtualPath), and the three destination sizes tile the object exactly - 0x1830 + 0xC8B0 = 0xE0E0, where the named Save_InitPartySnapshot documents the 0xC8B0-byte party snapshot at +0x1830 - so this reads a slot into memory; 'WriteSlotMeta' had the direction and the role wrong.

name: maybe_Ui_SetWidgetEnabled
summary: Vtable slot that enables/disables a widget: when the widget is still uninitialised (+0x14 clear) and the new state is 'on' it also raises the UI core's mode word at +0x94 (the cursor/selection flag), then forwards the flag to the object's own state setter, which never returns.
evidence: Only Ui_GetCore is named here; the setter it tail-calls (0x2912C6/0x0029126C) is still unnamed, so the exact meaning of the forwarded flag (enabled vs. visible) cannot be confirmed from the neighbourhood.

name: Anim_Owner_Tick
summary: Per-frame animation update of an object that owns one animation instance: if a pending transition is set at +0x108 it snaps the player to that frame first, then advances the embedded anim instance at +0xFC.
evidence: Both calls are now named - maybe_Anim_Player_SetFrame on the pending transition and Anim_Instance_Update on the embedded instance - which is exactly 'apply the pending frame, then tick the instance'; only the owning class is generic.

name: Ui_ClearChildrenAndDeleteSlot
signature: void Ui_ClearChildrenAndDeleteSlot(UiObject *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Tears a UI object down: detaches the six children tracked at +0xC (keeping the raw pointers, releasing the references) and then deletes the object whose handle sits at +0x48 through the UI core's non-clearing delete helper.
evidence: The first callee is now named maybe_Ui_DetachChildrenKeepRefs (0x215FC8), which calls the very same 0x21F8D0 delete helper this function uses for self+0x48, so the two halves are 'detach children' + 'delete the attached slot object' as the name says.

name: Gfx_Overlay_DrawBackdrop
signature: int* Gfx_Overlay_DrawBackdrop(OverlayCtx *self, u32 cmdArg, u32 arg3)
summary: Draws the full-screen backdrop quad (240x320) into the render command list and, unless the scene's 'skip overlay' bit (f_1346 bit 1) is set, submits it as a sorted element and flushes the buffer.
evidence: All drawing callees are now named (Gfx_GetRenderContext, Gfx_GpuCmd_FillSimple, maybe_Gfx_CmdList_GetSingleton, Gfx_SubmitSortedElement, Gfx_FlushCommandBuffer) and the quad size constants 0xF0 x 0x140 are literally the 3DS screen size, so 'draw the backdrop overlay' is exactly what the function does.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_SetSamplerState
summary: Selects the texture sampler parameters for a draw state: mode 0 writes filter 1 / 0x80 / wrap 6, modes 1 and 2 flip the wrap and filter bytes, then the state block is emitted into the GPU command stream and re-cached at state+4.
evidence: The PICA-style field values (0x80, 6, 1) selected by a small mode switch and the command emission Gfx_Pica_EmitDrawElements fit a sampler/texture-unit state write, but that callee name is itself only a low-confidence guess, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: Map_FindCellInDirection
signature: void Map_FindCellInDirection(u32 *out, int cell, u32 layer, u32 arg4, int *origin, int dir)
summary: Finds the map cell next to `cell` in the requested direction: decides which edge of the cell (+0x30/+0x34 range) faces the origin, and only if that matches the sign of `dir` resolves the neighbour through the layer lookup and hit-test chain; writes {index, cell} or {0xFFFFFFFF, 0} when there is none.
evidence: The direction/edge arithmetic is self-contained and the tail now calls the named maybe_Map_SearchCellRecord and Ui_HitTestRows on the same layer object, i.e. 'resolve the neighbouring cell in this direction' - exactly what the first pass proposed.

name: Ui_DataPanel_CreateGlobals
summary: Lazily creates the three global UI objects behind a one-byte 'already created' flag: a small 0x1C-byte helper (vtable 0x782950), the 0x7F4F1C-byte UI manager (vtable 0x782928) and the 0x2FB28-byte data-panel window whose 31 slot records of 0x12EC are constructed in place (vtable 0x764B84), then resets the window state.
evidence: The final call is the named Ui_Window_ResetState, whose summary names 'the 31 per-slot sub-widgets, the data-panel block at 0x24a98 and the fade block at 0x2fb18' - those are exactly the fields inside the 0x2FB28-byte object this function builds (31 * 0x12EC = 0x24AE4), and the three lazy-create guards are the classic 'construct-on-first-use' globals, so this creates them rather than freeing a slot as the old header claimed.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_RebuildSlotPages
summary: Rebuilds the cached text page of every one of the 31 UI slot records (0x12EC bytes each): builds the page from the data-manager record, and for the first slot also walks its 24 item slots (+0xEC array, 0xFFFF = empty), resolves each item and sets the matching bit (and the bits of its variants) in the 0x168-byte item-ownership bitmask at +0x4B30.
evidence: The body does no glyph-width work at all - it calls Text_Page_BuildFromRecord once per record, Item_LookupRecord on the 24 u16 item ids and writes `mask[id>>5] |= 1<<(id&31)` into the documented ownership bitmask at +0x4B30, so 'MeasureAllNameWidths' was wrong; the 31-record layout is the one Ui_Window_ResetState documents for the data-panel window, but why the item pass only runs for slot 0 is still unexplained, so it stays a maybe_.

name: Map_FindCellInDirectionEx
signature: void Map_FindCellInDirectionEx(u32 *out, u32 x, u32 y, int *origin, int dir)
summary: Coordinate form of the directional cell search: resolves the cell at (x,y), requires it to be a walkable, populated cell (flag +0x38 == 1, count +0x20 > 0), tests the direction against its edge range, and then writes {cell, cellPtr, containedActor} when the neighbour check passes.
evidence: Its only caller is now named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode (0x5F3AF0, 0.55), which walks a trail follower to the next walkable cell; the resolved cell/actor triple it returns is what that walker consumes, and it shares maybe_Map_SearchCellRecord and Ui_HitTestRows with 0x002D7DDC, so 'find the neighbouring cell in direction' is the right role.

name: maybe_Map_FindCellInDirectionAlt
signature: void maybe_Map_FindCellInDirectionAlt(u32 *out, int cell, u32 x, u32 y, int *origin, int dir)
summary: Third variant of the directional cell search: same edge test, but it additionally looks up the cell attributes 0xF and 0x10 and follows the small short at cell+0x1C+offset to pick the layer index before the hit test.
evidence: It is called from the named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode together with the other two direction finders, so the family is right, but the 0xF/0x10 attribute lookups and the short at +0x1C are still unexplained and decide which layer it picks - hence a maybe_.

name: Map_QueryCellRecord
signature: void Map_QueryCellRecord(u32 *out, u32 x, u32 y, u32 arg4)
summary: Resolves one map cell by (x,y) and writes {y, cell pointer, record pointer} into the caller's triple, requiring the cell to be walkable (flag +0x38 == 1) and populated (+0x20 > 0); on failure it writes the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel triple.

evidence: std_destroy_range's element destructor 0x3E04BC is the Ui_AnimRefList destructor (the ctor Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor is 0x3E0454, 0x68 bytes earlier) and it is applied to 12 entries of 0x50 bytes, followed by the named Ui_Object_DtorBase - so this is a destructor of an object owning twelve anim-ref lists ('PastPlaceWindow' was an unverified class guess).

name: maybe_Gfx_Actor_SpawnEffectSprite
summary: Resolves a handle to an actor (rejecting anything that is not an Actor subclass), builds a world position from the actor's +0x9C/+0xA0/+0xA4 origin plus the probe's float offsets with a 2.0 radius, and asks the scene to draw/spawn a sprite there with the given direction.

name: maybe_Field_Object_SelectIdleAnim
signature: void maybe_Field_Object_SelectIdleAnim(FieldObject *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)

evidence: The keyed-list select is now the named Container_KeyedList_Select and the record lookup is the named func_0035EB98 party accessor, so this selects an animation entry rather than 'stopping and releasing'; which of entries 1 and 8 means stand vs. swim is inferred from the flag, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_IsRowActivated
summary: Row predicate pair: asks the row object at index rowIndex through its virtual slot +0x20 whether it is active, and when the current row is different and valid it additionally asks the current row's slot +0x24 to compare itself with the candidate before answering 1.
evidence: The two-virtual protocol (slot +0x20 'active', slot +0x24 'compare with row') on the row-pointer array at +0x3C is clear, but neither the meaning of 'activated' nor the caller's use is confirmed by a named neighbour, so the name keeps its maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_SelectAnimEntry0
summary: Selects the first entry of the actor's keyed animation list: runs the shared prologue 0x005E7818 and then calls Container_KeyedList_Select(self+0x60, 0, 1) - i.e. play animation key 0 immediately.
evidence: The callee is now the named Container_KeyedList_Select and the body is exactly 'prologue + select key 0', which is how the neighbouring 0x00377398 switches animations (with keys 1 and 8); the 'ActionList_Rebuild' wording was wrong, and the owning class is still a guess.

name: Battle_RefreshUnitTextSlots
signature: void Battle_RefreshUnitTextSlots(BattleScene *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)

name: maybe_Model_Actor_UpdateAttachment
summary: Updates the model actor's visible attachment: looks the actor up in the battle weapon lists (+0x4254, then +0x4270), hides the attachment while the model is fading in, and creates or re-targets the attachment at +0x71C whenever its two cached ids (+0x71E / +0x722) no longer match.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetupChild
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_SetupChild(UiChild *self, UiWindow *parent, u32 id, int arg4, int arg5)

evidence: The layout-resolve call on parent+0x14 followed by a vtable+0xC hand-off is consistent with 'set up this child under that parent', but 0x0053649C is still unnamed, so the direction of the setup (and hence the exact wording) is not proven.

name: Ui_Window_SelectChildListEntry
summary: Selects one entry in the list the window exposes through its virtual slot +0x58: the entry id is combined with the window's high word ((id << 16) | index, the same convention as every other list call) and handed to the list's select-by-id.

name: maybe_Ui_RecordWindow_CountByCategory
summary: Recounts the seen records for the window's category tabs: clears the twenty per-category counters at +0x24 and the total at +0xC4, walks the 590 rows of the data-manager table, keeps the rows whose bit is set in the seen bitset at work+0x2A2C8 and increments the counter indexed by the row's kind byte.
evidence: The seen-bitset at work+0x2A2C8 and the row lookup 0x0063E998 are the same pair the book/database screens use, so 'count the seen records per category' is right; the counter index comes from an Item_LookupRecord row's +0x0C kind byte, and 590 rows does not match the whole item table, so which book this is stays open (maybe_).

name: Casino_Slot_ApplyRowState
summary: Resets the slot machine's five reel rows and then creates their icon sprites for one display state: Ui_HitIcon_ClearAllSlots on each of the five 0x238-byte rows at +0x5C0, then Ui_HitIcon_CreateSprites(row, index, state).
evidence: Both callees are now named (Ui_HitIcon_ClearAllSlots and Ui_HitIcon_CreateSprites) and take exactly the five rows at +0x5C0 with stride 0x238 and the state argument, so 'apply a row state to all five reels' is confirmed.

name: Ui_List_SetupRowWindows
signature: void Ui_List_SetupRowWindows(UiListRows *self, int **table, int **end, u32 count)
summary: Builds the visible row widgets of a list: initialises the row pool, stores the row count at +0x2C8, and for each entry of the two packed tables allocates a 0x1720-byte row window, creates its parts from the table and links it into the list at +0x11C.
evidence: The pool init is now named maybe_Ui_List_InitPool and each row is a 0x1720-byte window built with the named Ui_StampWindow_Ctor / Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable pair, so this creates row windows; the wording changed to 'SetupRowWindows' because the plain Ui_List_SetupRows name is already taken by 0x0023EDA0 (the ten-row list widget), a different function.

name: maybe_Ui_SkillPanel_IsDetailOpen
summary: One-liner global query: returns the UI flag byte at game work+0x2767D, which the skill panel's input and state handlers test before opening the detail view.
evidence: Still only read by the skill-panel handlers and no other function in the readable tree touches +0x2767D, but the body takes a value from an unrecovered register (in_r3) and the flag's actual meaning is not documented anywhere, so it stays at 0.3.

name: Ui_SkillPanel_OnTabChange
summary: Skill-panel tab handler: on the input flag it feeds the command to the member tab strip at +0x224 and stores the newly selected party member id in msg+0x11, and on cancel it either writes the pending message 0x17 and clears the UI busy word, or pushes the panel's confirm pane when the selected member has data.
evidence: The selected id now comes from the named Party_GetNextMemberId(self+0x224) and the pane push is the named Ui_SkillPanelWindow_PushPane, so the 'one tab per party member' reading of the tab handler is confirmed by the callees.

name: maybe_Ui_SkillPanel_HandleCommand
summary: Small command handler of the skill panel: command 0x13 shows and 0x14 hides the part at +0x1BC, and command 0x15 builds a message record (state 2 or 6 depending on the panel byte +0x2566), applies it to the block at +0x84C, confirms a part and pushes the next pane.
evidence: It is an entry of the same handler table (0x0072A158) as the confirmed tab handler and the codes are dispatched from the command byte, so 'command handler' is right, but nothing shows they are debug commands (the first pass's label), hence a maybe_ with the neutral wording.

name: Ui_SelectListWindow_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the select-list window: installs vtable 0x768664, destroys its six 0x50-byte animation-reference entries at +0x74 and runs the UI object base destructor.
evidence: The destroy helper is now named std_destroy_range with the anim-ref-list destructor 0x3E04BC as element destructor (six 0x50-byte entries), followed by Ui_Object_DtorBase, and the caller is the past-place window destructor named in N_026 - the dtor role is confirmed.

name: maybe_Data_FindNextRowMatchingConditions
summary: Advances the cursor to the next row of the 0x14-byte data table whose conditions hold: skips rows whose type byte does not match, requires the row's flag/seen bits, then walks the row's compact condition list (codes 0x19..0x22) comparing each byte against the selected party member's record fields, and leaves the index at cursor+4 (or the 0xFF/0x7F end marker).
evidence: The body is a condition evaluator over the named party-member accessor func_0035EB98 and the work flags at +0x27508, so 'find the next row whose conditions pass' is the honest description; the old 'Actor_FindNextEntryForCharacter' guessed the table's owner, which is not proven, and the twin 0x003AF808 scans the sibling array.

name: Container_List_ReleaseAll
summary: Empties an intrusive list: walks from the sentinel, unlinks every node from both neighbours and frees it, leaving the payload untouched - the generic 'clear this list and free the nodes' helper used by menu views, screen views and the camera.
evidence: The unlink-and-free loop is unambiguous and its callers (maybe_Ui_MenuView_Reset, Gfx_InitScreenViews, Camera_Reset) are reset paths that must drop their node lists, so the name holds; it is pure container code with no game semantics.

name: Container_ReleaseListNodes
summary: Destroys the nodes of the two intrusive lists the object owns (heads at +8 and +0x14, first nodes at +0xC and +0x18) by calling each node's virtual destructor (vtable slot +4).
evidence: The two-list walk with vtable slot +4 per node is explicit, and the callers are the model part-list rebuilders that must drop the old nodes before rebuilding - the generic 'release the nodes' role is confirmed.

name: Ui_ItemRow_Format
signature: void Ui_ItemRow_Format(UiRow *self, u32 itemId, int selected)
summary: Fills an item row: resolves the item's name (0x0063D338) and its icon group (0x0063D384 via the bag helper 0x0066AF08), picks the icon/texture for the group, copies the description into the shared line buffer while stripping CR/LF, and writes the icon, the name and the description into the row's three panes; the selected flag also updates the row's highlight byte.
evidence: Callees now include the named Ui_GetCore (texture resolution) and Game_GetDataManager, and the three writes at the end are the standard pane setter for slots 0/1/3 of the row's child index - exactly icon/name/description formatting.

name: Ui_SetNullButtonVisible
summary: Shows or hides the window pane named 'null_btn': resolves the pane by name through the layout object's virtual slot +0x2C and sets bit 0 of its flag byte to the requested state.
evidence: The literal s_null_btn passed to the layout lookup and the single visible-bit write make both the pane and the action certain; the only unnamed piece is the layout object's lookup slot.

name: maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_ScrollList_MoveCursorWithPage(void *self, int delta, u32 arg3, int pageCount)
summary: Page-aware cursor mover for a scrolling list: adds the delta to the row index, clamps it with the item count, then, when the last page is only partly filled, recomputes the page start/size and re-selects the entry before refreshing the rows.
evidence: The visible half matches the sibling 0x006E51E4 and ends in the named Ui_List_SelectEntryById, but the body is truncated by 'bad instruction data' and uses an unrecovered register (unaff_r6), so the page-clamping branch cannot be trusted - confidence stays at 0.3.

name: Ui_Row_RefreshValue
summary: Re-resolves a row's displayed value and re-renders it: remembers the old value, advances the row to its valid entry, stores the new value, renders and returns 1 only when the value actually changed so the caller can skip dependent work.
evidence: Both callees are now named (maybe_Ui_Result_AdvanceToValidRow and Ui_Row_Render), which shows this is a refresh-and-report-change helper; the old 'OnValueChanged' name suggested a notification handler rather than the refresh itself.

name: Ui_Row_SetIndex
summary: Sets the row's entry index: when it differs from the stored one it writes the index, marks the row dirty (0xB), re-resolves the value, toggles the visible bit of the two optional child panes (the 'empty/extra' indicators) and finally re-renders the row.
evidence: The body only touches the row's own index/value/child-pane fields and ends in the named Ui_Row_Render through the named maybe_Ui_Result_AdvanceToValidRow, so 'set index and re-render' is confirmed.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_ExecCommand
summary: Executes one slot-machine presentation command: refreshes the payout/value display, resets the five rows, hides the symbols, stores the requested configuration bytes, and when the pending flag is clear and its timer expired it starts the win presentation, applies the row state and moves the machine to step 5 or 8.
evidence: The callees are now all named Casino_Slot_* helpers (reset rows, hide symbols, stop all reels, apply row state) plus the state-machine setter func_003280C0, so this is a slot-machine command executor; the old 'ExecState' wording hid that it reads a command struct, but the exact command is not identified.

name: Ui_ReleaseSubObject
summary: Releases the sub-object referenced by slot word [1] through the UI core's heap and clears the slot, returning the slot so callers can chain; a template copy of the same body lives at 0x003D2DFC.
evidence: The free is the UI heap release used elsewhere for UI children and the slot word is cleared immediately; the only unknown is which class owns the slot, which does not matter for this generic release helper.

name: Model_BindVariantResources
summary: Binds one resource-set variant to a model: fills a small bind descriptor with the resource-set tags (0x782244/0x782254), binds the variant through Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant using the model's render object, applies it with the model's bind-set call and releases the temporary bindings.
evidence: The binder is now named Gfx_BindResourceSetVariant and the descriptor tags are the resource-set constants, so 'bind the variant resource set to this model' is exactly what happens; the trailing Gfx_MaterialSet_Release calls are the cleanup of the temporary descriptor.

name: Model_BindSingleResource
summary: Binds a single resource to the model's dedicated binding slot at +0x68: clearing the resource unbinds it, otherwise the old texture binding is released, the new one is bound through Gfx_BindSingleResource and, on success, the render object switches to slot +0x68.
evidence: The body calls the named Gfx_BindSingleResource and Gfx_TextureBinding_Release on a fixed slot, with a clear 'unbind when res == 0' branch - the role is unambiguous.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_BuildMemberActionEntries
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_BuildMemberActionEntries(BattleUiContext *self, BattleActor *actor, u32 actionId, u32 flags)
summary: Fills the next free entry of the battle HUD table (48 entries of 0x90 bytes at +0x4AF) for one of the six action slots of an actor: finds a free slot, checks the actor against the slot's type byte, copies the 0x58-byte display block, stores the actor pointer and validity byte and spawns the balloon when the battle UI is active.
evidence: The balloon spawn is the named Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor and the row lookup the named maybe_Text_FindRowIndexByType, so 'build one HUD entry per actor action' is well supported; whether these are damage numbers or action labels is not proven, so the name keeps a maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_BuildMemberActionEntriesB
summary: Damaged second copy of the HUD entry builder 0x003C3F5C: writes the actor pointer, the 0x58-byte display block and the validity byte into the 0x60-stride entry array and spawns a balloon, but the loop head and most operands come from unrecovered registers.
evidence: Same stores and the same Ui_Balloon_SpawnAtAnchor call as 0x003C3F5C, but the body uses unaff_r4..r11 and stack arguments, i.e. damaged decompilation, so only the family can be stated - hence 0.25.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActorsB
summary: Second actor-to-widget link pass: for the party list at battle work+0x4260, the sibling list at +0x427C and the four unit lists at +0x4298, it matches each entry's actor handle against the UI's actor list and calls the widget's vtable slot +0x98 (bind) when they match, with a unit-kind filter for the enemy lists.
evidence: It shares the list walk, the tagged-handle resolution and the vtable+0x98 bind with 0x003C4D9C, and it now calls the named Battle_IsUnitKindShownInMemberUi to skip units that the member UI does not show; the two copies are near-duplicates, so which one is the 'B' pass is only a label.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActors
summary: Links live battle actors to their HUD widgets: walks the party list at battle work+0x4260 and the sibling list at +0x427C, resolves each entry's handle through the tagged object table (0x7B80C0), compares the actor/UI ids and calls the widget's vtable slot +0x98 to bind the actor.
evidence: The handle table and the vtable+0x98 bind are the same ones the confirmed member-UI code uses (0x003C64FC is the near-duplicate), so 'link member actors' is the right role; the exact event that triggers the pass is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_TitleMessage_ReleaseChild
summary: Frees the child object referenced by slot word [1] through the UI heap and clears the slot; byte-for-byte the same body as 0x003BC520, i.e. a template copy of the generic 'release sub-object' helper.
evidence: Same body as the confirmed Ui_ReleaseSubObject (0x003BC520) - same UI heap free and slot clear - and its callers are UI teardown paths, so the action is certain but the title-message ownership is only a class hint.

name: Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateModel
summary: Refreshes the 3D character model shown by a status/equipment window: reapplies the label text group, resets the model's extra state and re-applies the equipment grip slot and grip state.
evidence: The callees are now named Model_Equip_SetGripSlot, Model_Equip_UpdateGripState and Ui_TextLabel_SetTextGroup, all applied to the model object at +0x22C, so 'update the displayed model' is confirmed.

name: Field_ObjectSprite_Setup
summary: Places a field object sprite from its map record: copies the flags/colour/scale, builds the rotation quaternion, sets the sprite transform and handle slot, resolves the record's kind-9 sub-record for the bounds (falling back to the record's own extents) and stores the resulting position/bounds for later region picking.
evidence: The callees are now named Math_BuildQuaternionFromEuler, Field_ObjectSprite_SetTransform, maybe_Field_ObjectSprite_SetHandleSlot and Field_Object_GetKind9Record, so the object is a field sprite initialised from a record rather than specifically a 'talk balloon'.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_RefreshForSpeaker
summary: Refreshes a slot table for the current speaker: derives the speaker id, re-rolls the random entries, then looks through the ten slots for the one whose id matches the active map record and selects/applies it (falling back to the table's currently selected entry).
evidence: All four callees are now named (Ui_SlotTable_RollRandomEntries, Ui_SlotTable_GetSelectedId, maybe_Ui_SlotTable_SelectEntry, maybe_Ui_SlotTable_ApplyEntry), so the refresh role is right; the 'NoRecord' wording of the first pass described the missing record argument, not the behaviour, and the id comparison against the map record at +0x1C is only partly decoded.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_Pick3D
summary: 3D hit-test over a list of axis-aligned float boxes: takes the current scene position, expands each box by half its size on every axis and returns the id byte stored in the first box that contains the position, or 0.
evidence: The position read is now the named Field_SceneNode_GetPosition on the UI overlay object, and the 6-float boxes with an id byte at +0x18 are self-contained; whether the owner is a 'slot table' is still the first pass's guess, so it stays a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotTable_Pick2D
summary: 2D point-in-rectangle hit test over a list of short {x, y, w, h, id} records: compares the current 2D sprite position (expanded by a two-pixel margin) against each normalised rectangle and returns the id of the first match.
evidence: The record layout and the sprite-size read are clear, but the body uses an unrecovered register (unaff_r11) inside the rectangle normalisation, i.e. damaged decompilation, so the name and confidence stay low.

name: maybe_Ui_DebugLabel_SetParamText
summary: Shows the current debug parameter value on a UI label: formats work+0x27C7C as decimal into the global debug string buffer (0x7AC834+0x848), points the buffer's cursor at it and sets the label's pane image to resource 0x21.
evidence: The value source (work+0x27C7C), the decimal format and the global debug buffer are all visible, and the tail is the standard pane-image setter; that the label is a debug readout is still an inference from the buffer, hence a maybe_.

name: Model_ReapplyStateBytes
summary: Re-applies the character model's two equipment-state bytes: runs the weapon-node attach step, then for the grip node at self+0x6E4 reads each of the two state bytes (+0x60 main, +0x61 for the secondary grip resolved via the item id at +0x4C) and re-sets the corresponding grip node.
evidence: The callees are now named Model_Equip_AttachWeaponNode and Model_Equip_SetGripNode, and the item id at +0x4C is resolved with Item_LookupRecord before the secondary grip is re-applied, so 'reapply the grip state bytes' is confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_DebugLabel_SetTextEx
summary: Sibling of 0x003E9E60: resolves the caller's value to an item-storage pointer, formats it into the global debug string buffer and sets the label's pane image to resource 0x1F.
evidence: Same debug-buffer + pane-image sequence as 0x003E9E60, with the value derived through the named Item_GetStoragePointer; the label's purpose is still an inference, so it keeps a maybe_.

name: maybe_Item_IsRecipeCraftable
signature: u32 maybe_Item_IsRecipeCraftable(WorkData *self, int recipeIndex, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Checks one crafting recipe against the player's storage: takes the 0x10-byte recipe entry (material count plus a relative pointer to the u16 material ids) and returns 0 as soon as Item_GetStoragePointer cannot resolve one of the materials.
evidence: The material check is now known to be Item_GetStoragePointer on each u16 id of the 0x10-byte entry, so 'can this recipe be crafted' is the right reading; the body still takes one operand from a recovered call result (extraout_r1), so the recipe-bounds test is not fully trustworthy.

name: Item_AreAllRecipesCraftable
signature: u32 Item_AreAllRecipesCraftable(WorkData *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Returns 1 only when every one of the first ten crafting recipes is craftable: it runs the same per-recipe material check as 0x0063ECF0 and bails out with 0 as soon as one recipe has a missing material.
evidence: Control flow fixes the meaning: the shared LAB returns 0 when the current recipe failed, the counter only advances on success and the function returns 1 after the tenth entry - so it is an AND over the recipes and the old 'IsAnyRecipeCraftable' was the opposite of what the code does; the material check is the named Item_GetStoragePointer.

name: maybe_Item_GetStoragePointerWithInit
summary: Resolves an item's storage pointer, first lazily creating the global 0x2FB28-byte UI window that owns the storage (31 slot records of 0x12EC bytes, vtable 0x764B84) when the one-byte 'already created' flag says it does not exist yet.
evidence: The tail is the named Item_GetStoragePointer on the 0x7BE320 window, preceded by the same construct-on-first-use block as 0x00623B48 (which builds that exact window) - so this is a lazy-init wrapper, and the old 'CheckMaterialAvailability' described a material count that does not exist in the body.

name: Ui_StatusParamWindow_ToggleMemberRow
summary: Frame tick of the status window's alternating member display: counts down the 60-frame timer at +0x17C and, when it reaches zero, flips the row index at +0x178 between 0 and 1, points the pane at the matching 0x44-byte member record (+0xF4 + index*0x44) and reloads the timer.
evidence: The exact 0x3C-frame period, the 0/1 index flip and the 0x44-stride member records at +0xF4 are all visible, and its callers are the tactics-window handlers (including the confirmed Ui_SakusenWindow_CloseDetail) that use it to hide the extra row - so 'toggle the member row' is confirmed.

name: Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshMemberIds
summary: Rebuilds the battle party panel's id lists: clears the 31-entry main and spare id arrays and the four-slot shortlist, walks the party member list, fills the main array with every member id, splits off the reserve members and the first four usable actors and finally updates the icon row and the target window's slots.
evidence: Callees are now named (maybe_Party_IsReserveMember, maybe_Ui_TargetWindow_SetSlotCharacter, Ui_Element_SetFlagBit0) and the 0xFF-filled arrays plus the party member accessor func_0035EB98 pin down the rebuild.

name: Container_ArrayCtor
summary: Constructor of a small container: zeroes the three-word header and default-constructs a fixed array of seven 0x50-byte elements at +0xC using the element constructor 0x00326838.
evidence: The body is exactly a header clear plus std_ConstructArray(self+3, element ctor 0x00326838, 0x50, 7) and it is called from two object constructors - the 'array container ctor' role is confirmed, only the element type is unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_InitTwoFixedArrays
summary: Constructs the two fixed arrays of seven 0x50-byte elements at +0xC and +0x23C with the shared element constructor 0x0032686C and returns the object base.
evidence: Both calls are the same construct-range helper with the same element type and count as 0x004066DC (one 7-array), so 'initialise two fixed 7-element arrays' is certain; the 'gauge segment / slot window' meaning of the elements is still the first pass's guess, hence the neutral name and a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_CreateFromDefsB
summary: Creates a message-window variant from two definition blocks: builds a 5-word layout descriptor from def1 and a 2-word one from def2, constructs the window through 0x002D97E8, installs vtable 0x76D070 and clears its state bytes.
evidence: The two descriptor literals (0x782524 / 0x782234) and the constructor + vtable store are visible, and the vtable's slots are the 0x265004 message functions; the concrete variant is still not identifiable, so the name stays a maybe_.

name: Ui_Widget_Ctor_vt7781EC
summary: Constructor of a small UI widget: runs the base constructor 0x17C1C8, installs vtable 0x7781EC, initialises the member pair at +0x48 (secondary vtable 0x75B1D0 with a back-pointer) and default-constructs its four 0x18-byte elements at +0x6C.
evidence: Base ctor + vtable literal + Ui_Object_InitMemberPair + std_ConstructArray(..., 0x18, 4) is a textbook constructor; the vtable suffix stays because the class has no other identifying strings.

name: Actor_HandleRef_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of the tiny helper object that stores an actor handle: runs the shared base init and installs the class vtable; its methods forward virtual calls to the actor resolved from the stored handle.
evidence: The installed vtable is now the named symbol g_actorHandleRefVtable, and the sibling methods in the same 0x4AF2CC..0x4AF5xx block dispatch handle -> +0x7C/+0x80/+0x84, so the class identity is confirmed.

name: Field_ObjectCtor_vt76D7FC
summary: Constructor of a field object from the shared object pool: installs vtable 0x76D7FC, seeds the two inverted default vectors, the id/flip/alpha defaults (0, 3, 0xFF), then constructs the embedded sprite at +0x1C and its default fields; returns the object base 0x70 bytes before the sprite.
evidence: The embedded constructor is now named Field_ObjectSprite_CtorBase, so this is an object ctor that owns a field sprite (the old 'CreateNode' suggested a leaf node); which object kind it is, is expressed by the vtable suffix.

name: Field_ObjectCtor_vt77034C
summary: Constructor of a field object variant: installs vtable 0x77034C, sets the id/flag bytes (+0x45 = 1, +0x46 = 0xFF, +0x47 = 0) and constructs the embedded field scene-object sprite at +0x48, returning the enclosing base.
evidence: The sub-constructor is now named Field_SceneObjectSprite_Ctor, so this builds an object around a scene-object sprite; the sibling 0x0040CF0C sets the same id bytes to the empty sentinels but has a different vtable (0x76D7D4), so 'Type1' was only an ordinal.

name: maybe_Field_ObjectCtor_vt76D7D4
summary: Constructor of the small field-object variant: installs vtable 0x76D7D4 and seeds its id/layer fields with the 'none' sentinels (id byte 0xFF, u16 0xFFFF, word 0, byte 0xFF) so the object reads as unplaced.
evidence: Same base init + vtable + sentinel pattern as the sibling field-object constructors (one of which now constructs the named Field_SceneObjectSprite_Ctor), but this variant has no embedded sprite call and no named caller beyond the object-table builder, so the name keeps a maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_InteractJob_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the field interaction job object (the worker that walks the hero to an NPC/object and runs the interaction): installs vtable 0x775558 and sets the initial state bytes (+0x45 = 1, +0x46 = 0xFF).
evidence: The vtable it installs is the one the 0x4A3A18 'InteractJob begin' body and the 0x4A3B3C destructor belong to, so the family is right; those siblings are themselves only maybe_ names, so the class label stays unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_ValueHolder_Ctor
summary: In-place constructor of a tiny object that holds one float: base init, installs vtable 0x77635C and writes the sentinel -1000.0f to +0x48 (the 'no value yet' marker read by its only other method).
evidence: The single float member with the -1000.0f sentinel and the vtable 0x77635C are clear, but neither the class name nor what the value drives (its sibling copies it into a game-work float) identifies a 'value holder', so it keeps a maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_Ctor_vt77C298
summary: Constructor of a pooled object: installs vtable 0x77C298, clears the state bytes at +0x46/+0x47 and sets the id byte at +0x45 to 0xFF (the empty id used by this object family).
evidence: The body is the same 'pool create + vtable + id sentinel' pattern as the field-object constructors, and the first pass's 'floor-map jump trigger' label has no support in the body, so the vtable is used as the discriminator and the name stays a maybe_.

name: Casino_Poker_DealHandA
summary: Deals one five-card poker hand: shuffles the 13-entry suit/rank table and the 4-entry aux table, moves deck cards into the five hand slots (the first one from a random deck position, the rest via the slot exchange helper), then shuffles the hand window and rotates the visible slots.
evidence: All four helpers are now named Casino_Poker_ShuffleDeck13 / ShuffleDeck4 / ShuffleU16 / maybe_Casino_Poker_RotateHandSlots, and the body is one deal pass over the five 2-byte hand slots, so 'deal a hand' is confirmed (the 'A' variant suffix is kept for the sibling copies).

name: maybe_Casino_Poker_DealHandD
summary: Poker deal variant driven by a rank-chance roll: shuffles both deck tables, then deals the first three hand slots from either the top of the deck or a random position depending on Casino_Poker_RollHandRankChance, deals the remaining three slots from fixed deck positions and rotates the hand.
evidence: The family is confirmed by the named shuffle/roll helpers, but the branch on Casino_Poker_RollHandRankChance means this is not a plain deal - it is the 'rigged/extra-chance' deal variant, and which game mode uses it is unknown.

name: maybe_Casino_Poker_RotateHandSlots
summary: Reorders the dealt poker hand: draws a random count 0..5 from the game RNG, swaps that many 2-byte hand slots between the two halves of the hand array, then shuffles the first half, the second half and the whole hand window again.
evidence: The swap loop and the three named Casino_Poker_ShuffleU16 calls are clear, and its nine callers are all in the poker-deal block, but the swap count is taken from a lost call result (extraout_r1), so the exact reordering cannot be verified.

name: maybe_Battle_ShowCommandListEntry
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ShowCommandListEntry(BattleScene *self, int entryIndex, int visible, u32 arg4)
summary: Shows or hides one row of the battle command list: hiding row N (or the 0xFF 'none' row) sets the actor-list entry for that command visible flag, while showing the special row 4 either forwards to the window's own vtable slot +0x60 or to the shared actor action handler depending on the window's state byte +0x168D.
evidence: The actor list it pokes (battle work+0x4254) is the same one the member-UI code uses and the state byte at +0x168D is read twice to choose the handler, so the 'show/hide a command entry' role holds; the exact meaning of rows 4 and 0xFF is not proven.
